children: ASML
is returning more capital to shareholders, declaring an
interim dividend of 1.88 per ordinary share
for fiscal 2026 while continuing an aggressive multi-billion-euro share repurchase program.
The Dutch semiconductor equipment giant said the dividend will be
payable on Nov. 4, 2026
The payout comes alongside significant buyback activity.
ASML said it repurchased roughly
4.1 billion worth of shares in the third quarter
under its current 20262028 share buyback program.
That combination of dividends and buybacks highlights the strength of ASML's cash-generation profile at a time when AI-related semiconductor demand continues to stretch its production capacity.
The company recently reported
11.7 billion in third-quarter net sales
and about
5 billion in net income
, while management said demand for its chipmaking equipment is likely to exceed supply through at least 2028.
That backdrop matters because ASML is simultaneously being asked to invest heavily in additional production while returning substantial amounts of capital to investors.

The company's lithography systems remain critical to advanced semiconductor manufacturing, giving ASML unusual pricing power and visibility as chipmakers expand capacity for AI, logic and memory applications.
Investor Takeaway
I think the dividend itself is not the main story.
The bigger signal is that ASML can continue
returning billions of euros to shareholders while still funding capacity expansion
The 4.1 billion of Q3 repurchases is especially notable because buybacks can have a much larger impact on per-share earnings than the relatively modest interim dividend.
For investors, the key things to watch are
free cash flow, buyback pace, dividend growth and how much additional capital ASML needs to spend to expand supply through 2028 and beyond
If AI-related demand stays strong and margins remain near current levels, ASML could continue combining growth investment with substantial shareholder returns.
That is a powerful setup, but the balance matters: the company still needs enough capital to remove the production bottlenecks currently limiting future sales.

title: ASML Makes a Massive Move to Reward Shareholders
